cards.text: Jesus moves on from there and spots a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. Friend, NOBODY walks past a tax booth thinking, "Ooh, let me go make a new friend over there." Jesus does.

cards.question: Jesus sees Matthew sitting at his tax booth. What does Jesus tell him?
When Jesus calls him, Matthew asks for some time to think it over first.

cards.text: NOPE. Matthew gets up and follows Him, just like that. Friend, I have taken longer deciding which side of the dough to stamp.

cards.question: Later, Jesus is dining at Matthew's house with His disciples. Who comes and eats with them?

cards.text: Matthew's house is PACKED. Then the Pharisees, a group of religious leaders, see who Jesus is eating with, and oh, they have QUESTIONS.

cards.question: The Pharisees take their question about the dinner at Matthew's house straight to Jesus.

cards.text: Nope, they go to His disciples: “Why does your Teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?” Jesus hears it, and He answers with a picture from everyday life.

cards.question: Jesus says it's not the healthy who need a doctor. It's the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’” Homework, assigned on the SPOT.

cards.question: Jesus says He has not come to call the righteous. He has come to call ___.

cards.text: Then a new group walks up: John's disciples, the followers of John the Baptist. They've got a question about fasting, and they bring the Pharisees into it too.

cards.question: John's disciples say that Jesus's disciples fast more often than they do.

cards.text: Right, it's the other way around: John's disciples and the Pharisees fast often, and Jesus's disciples don't. Jesus replies, “How can the guests of the bridegroom mourn while He is with them?”

cards.question: Jesus says the guests can't mourn while the bridegroom is with them. But what time does He say will come?

answers.text: The time the bridegroom is taken from them
The time the guests are all sent home
The time the wedding is called off

cards.text: And then, Jesus says, they will fast. Next picture: an old garment, and friend, after years in a junk drawer, I take old and worn out PERSONALLY.

cards.question: Jesus says no one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. Why not?

answers.text: The patch pulls away and the tear gets worse
The patch is too small to cover the hole
The new cloth fades faster than the old

cards.text: Then one more picture: new wine poured into old wineskins. I bet you can already see where this one's headed.

cards.question: Jesus says pouring new wine into old wineskins makes the skins burst.
Instead, Jesus says, new wine goes into ___ wineskins, and ___ are preserved.

findings.problem: The opening card begins "Jesus moves on from there," but never says where "there" is or what just happened. The passage starts in the middle of the flow, right after the paralytic is healed in Matthew 9:1-8. The card also doesn't say what is going on before the call.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card tells verse 10 ("Matthew's house is PACKED") but cites only Matthew 9:11. The citation should be Matthew 9:10-11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "Matthew's house is PACKED" is narration, not a joke, and it stretches verse 10. The text says only that many tax collectors and sinners came and ate with Him.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "Homework, assigned on the SPOT" is a school joke. It is also pointed at Jesus's own words, which brushes against the reverence rule.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids. Work, bosses and bills are fine.

findings.problem: The joke's target is Jesus's instruction to "go and learn what this means." The joke treats His teaching as something to laugh at, not the human situation of the people in the story.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.
